candidates.lead: Ronnie was diagnosed with aplastic anaemia just before his first birthday
candidates.evidence_text: An 18-month-old boy with a rare blood condition has been given "a second chance at life" after undergoing a life-saving stem cell transplant, his mum has said Ronnie, from Wirral on Merseyside, was diagnosed with aplastic anaemia - which is fatal if left untreated - a week before his first birthday in March last year He underwent the transplant after a suitable anonymous match was found in the US, with Ronnie's mum Laura saying: "I can't describe the feeling of what the donor did for our little boy." The 31-year-old said Ronnie was "doing absolutely amazing" back home after the transplant in August She said: "Thank you will never be enough for him [the donor], but I think to say it face to face and even if he was able to meet our little boy, that he's given a second chance at life, it would be amazing "But no words will ever show our appreciation for him."

candidates.lead: Women with endometriosis are suffering financially as well as physically, a new report by MPs warns
candidates.evidence_text: 'Some think endometriosis is just a bad period, but it's so much worse' - BBC News Image source, Megan Gomersall Image caption, Megan Gomersall has been out of work for about two and a half years because of her symptoms By James Fell and Mat Trewern , North West Published 15 October 2026 Women with endometriosis are being forced out of work, losing income and facing significant financial hardship because of the condition, according to a new report by MPs. The inquiry by the All-Party Parliamentary Group on Endometriosis, supported by Endometriosis UK, found 47% of women with the condition had lost income because of their symptoms, while 28% had left a job altogether. Among them was Chloe Ward, from Bolton, who said her endometriosis - which can cause severe pain, fatigue, heavy bleeding and fertility problems - had cost her thousands of pounds and affected her ability to run her own business. She said: "A lot of people think it's just a bad period, but it's so much worse." Image source, Chloe Ward Image caption, Chloe Ward says years of treatment, surgery and time off work have left her paying a heavy financial price for endometriosis About one in 10 women suffer from the condition, but diagnosis can be a lengthy process. Chloe said it took seven years for her to be diagnosed. She said being self-employed in the beauty industry meant she had flexibility, but no financial safety net. "If I'm not there to do the treatments, nobody pays me," she said. She told BBC Radio Manchester she had lost clients over the years because flare-ups could leave her unable to work at short notice. Chloe is now waiting for a hysterectomy, which will mean more time away from work. "There's so much to it that people don't understand," she said. The financial impact has extended beyond lost earnings. After receiving a stage-four endometriosis diagnosis in 2023, she paid about £6,000 for private surgery because NHS waiting times were too long. She and her partner also spent about £8,000 on a third round of IVF after two NHS-funded attempts failed. The report found 39% of women with endometriosis had experienced financial hardship because of the condition, while 40% said they had turned down career opportunities due to a lack of workplace support. Image source, Chloe Ward Image caption, Endo the Night encourages people to host fundraising events while raising awareness of endometriosis Megan Gomersall, 30, from Rochdale, said the condition ended a career she loved. The former paediatric nurse has been out of work for about two and a half years because of her symptoms. She said endometriosis, which affects her bladder and bowel, left her in severe pain during shifts and frequently off sick before she received a diagnosis. It took 13 years for her condition to be identified. "It has been really, really difficult," she said. "It's been like a grieving process in a way. I feel like I've completely lost my identity and purpose." Megan said she believed more could be done to help women remain in work through reasonable adjustments and greater awareness of the condition. The inquiry found fewer than half of employees with endometriosis had received workplace adjustments, while 94% believed employers lacked a good understanding of the condition. A Department of Health and Social Care spokesperson said endometriosis can have a "devastating impact" on women's lives and said the government's renewed Women's Health Strategy identifies it as a priority condition. The spokesperson said the findings highlighted the need for better support, both in healthcare and in the workplace. candidates.evidence_text: The Wanted's Max George says Tom Parker is 'always there' - BBC News Image source, PA Image caption, Tom Parker was diagnosed with an incurable brain tumour in 2020 By Anna Jameson and Georgie Docker , North West Published 15 October 2026 With four million singles and a million album sales under their belts, The Wanted were one of the biggest boy bands in the 2010s. After breaking through onto the music scene in America, the band enjoyed global success before tragedy struck when Bolton-born Tom Parker died from a brain tumour in 2022 at the age of 33. As band members Max George and Siva Kaneswaran set off on tour as The Wanted 2.0, George, from Swinton, in Manchester, spoke to BBC North West Tonight about Parker, returning to the stage as a two-piece, and going through heart surgery. He spoke ahead of The Wanted 2.0 performing at Manchester Academy on Friday. Image caption, The Wanted's Max George said hearing late bandmate Tom Parker's voice is his favourite part of being of stage The Wanted formed as a five-piece boy band in 2009, and had Max George, Siva Kaneswaran, Jay McGuiness, Tom Parker, and Nathan Sykes in the line-up. "It was a shock because I'd never, ever thought that I'd ever be in a band that was successful," George said. Image source, PA Image caption, Max George and Siva Kaneswaran performing together as The Wanted 2.0 The bandmembers had each been selected as part of a mass open audition held by talent manager Jayne Collins, who had also put together The Saturdays. "I was sort of in so I could afford just to have a few beers at the weekend, go out with my mates and put a roof over my head," George said. "That was my vision with it because I loved doing it." But in May 2011 the band released Glad You Came. It was the second single from their second album was released, and it changed everything. "All of a sudden it took off," George recalled. "Our record label rang me and said it was selling over 300,000 copies a week. "I was just mind-blown." He said the success in America brought the band a whole new level of fame. "It was life-changing," he said. "Obviously we'd had success here. "But when you get it on a scale somewhere as big as America, it really does change your life. "The number of people that come to see you and recognise you walking through New York... was just crazy." Image caption, The Wanted's first single All Time Low was released in 2010, putting them into the UK charts The band announced they were having a break in January 2014. Six years later, Parker was diagnosed with inoperable stage four glioblastoma. The Wanted released their first single in seven years in October 2021, followed by a greatest hits album the next month. After accompanying the band on a 12-date UK tour, Parker died in March 2022. "I think with any loss you have days that are terrible, but then weeks where you feel fine. And then all of a sudden you think 'Why have I not been upset the last few weeks? "I think that's just the way that you deal with stuff." George is currently embarking on tour with Kaneswaran. It is the second tour the pair have done since Parker's death. "I get reminded [of Tom] all the time," George said. "Me and Tom always used to be in each other's ears because we'd sing together on lead vocals. "I still have his voice playing in my ears when we're on stage. "He's always there which is lovely for me. I love that. "It's my favourite thing about doing the show." Image source, PA Image caption, The Wanted 2.0 are currently touring the UK on their (We're) Glad You Came tour Since The Wanted 2.0's first toured in America in 2024, George has been through a health scare of his own. Nearly two years ago, doctors discovered he had a blockage in his heart, requiring urgent surgery. "I had the pacemaker put in but then it became apparent that there was a mistake," he said. "That made me even worse. "So I had to have it removed and put back in and it took me about a year to get over it." He said he had to get through his illness, not just for himself, but for his family. "When you're so ill you're not really that scared yourself," George said. "You just feel out of it." "But when you see that look in your mum's eyes and you see what it's doing to her.. that's the bit that wakes you up and makes you think 'God, I have to get through this'. George added: "This is a whole new chapter with Siva. I love working, I love being on stage and forgetting about this stuff." The Wanted 2.0 kicked off their 2026 UK tour i

candidates.lead: The prime minister has been under growing pressure since the club was found guilty of Premier League rule breaches
candidates.evidence_text: Andy Burnham had two hospitality dinners with Manchester City football club's chairman while mayor of Greater Manchester, it has emerged The PM dined with Khaldoon Al Mubarak at matches in 2017 and 2018 - but this was not detailed in a statement on Monday by the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) about his meetings with the club Burnham has been under pressure to clarify his previous discussions with Man City since the club was found guilty of having "systematically" broken Premier League rules, which it will appeal The PM, who was mayor until June, sparked widespread controversy when he said last month he would be "really concerned" if the club's owners now sold up Separately, it has emerged that a representative from the club joined a trade mission to India this week alongside Burnham's successor as mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig The trade mission was organised by the business department, but as first reported in the Guardian, , external Manchester City's invitation came from the Great North, a coalition of Northern mayors and regional leaders

candidates.evidence_text: An 18-month-old boy with a rare blood condition has been given "a second chance at life" after undergoing a life-saving stem cell transplant, his mum has said Ronnie, from Wirral on Merseyside, was diagnosed with aplastic anaemia - which is fatal if left untreated - a week before his first birthday in March last year He underwent the transplant after a suitable anonymous match was found in the US, with Ronnie's mum Laura saying: "I can't describe the feeling of what the donor did for our little boy." The 31-year-old said Ronnie was "doing absolutely amazing" back home after the transplant in August She said: "Thank you will never be enough for him [the donor], but I think to say it face to face and even if he was able to meet our little boy, that he's given a second chance at life, it would be amazing "But no words will ever show our appreciation for him."

candidates.evidence_text: Women with endometriosis are being forced out of work, losing income and facing significant financial hardship because of the condition, according to a new report by MPs The inquiry by the All-Party Parliamentary Group on Endometriosis, supported by Endometriosis UK, found 47% of women with the condition had lost income because of their symptoms, while 28% had left a job altogether Among them was Chloe Ward, from Bolton, who said her endometriosis - which can cause severe pain, fatigue, heavy bleeding and fertility problems - had cost her thousands of pounds and affected her ability to run her own business She said: "A lot of people think it's just a bad period, but it's so much worse." About one in 10 women suffer from the condition, but diagnosis can be a lengthy process Chloe said it took seven years for her to be diagnosed

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Luke Littler mocked over what he did with his £39k BMW outside a Wigan leisure centre A fellow player jokingly accused him of parking 'like a t**t' Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter and Jack Fifield 05:50, 16 Oc Darts sensation Luke Littler has hit back after a fellow player accused him of parking his BWM 'like a t**t' in Wigan. The 19-year-old star's £39,000 custom-plate motor was spotted parked outside the Robin Park Leisure Centre in the town on October 4 - the day before he played at Fellow player Jackson King, 18, took a picture and posted it to the "Parking/Driving Like A Tw** in Wigan !" page on Facebook. "Park like a t*** Luke Littler edition," he wrote Warrington-born Littler, who is nicknamed 'The Nuke', responded saying: "Class that," before explaining in a reply: "No spaces mate so seen the car in front was on the gravel so thought I would join." Other commenters were divided on their opinion of the parking job. Joshua Fulton wrote: "The champ can park where he wants," while Ant Hayton wrote: "Did he park or land it?" Littler's 2025 BMW 120 M Sport, which he reportedly purchased for £39,000, has a top speed of 140 mph and can go from 0 to 60 in 7.8 seconds

candidates.evidence_text: Rusholme Leading Manchester school hits out at 'inaccurate' claims as police descend after violence erupts Xaverian College says 'we are aware of speculation and inaccurate information being shared online' Add to preferred sources Comments News Paul B A leading Manchester college has issued a new statement after police were called to a disturbance on its campus during an open day. Footage shared on social media showed police outside 164-year-old Xaverian College in Rusholme last Saturday afternoon Clips shared widely on TikTok showed groups of youths running across a large grassy area in front of the college building. Greater Manchester Police confirmed officers attended at around 1.10pm to reports of a fight and disturbance involving a number of youngers Xaverian College has now moved to provide more detail - and hit out at 'inaccurate information being shared online that does not reflect what happened' The college said there was an 'altercation' involving 'three young visitors, who are not students at the college'. They were removed from the campus. The college said no weapons were involved and there were thankfully no injuries. The college's next open day will go ahead as plan The college's statement said: "Towards the end of our open day on Saturday 10th October 2026, there was an altercation involving three young visitors, who are not students at the college. Staff responded immediately and the individuals were removed from campus

But the prosecution at Minshull Street Crown Court say Mr Richardson did not stop and put his foot down, dragging Mr Mullins, 56, Earlier in the trial, witnesses described seeing the Volvo ‘absolutely tanking it’ towards the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane. PC Mark Noonan, a forensic collision investigator for GMP, showed the jury a number of CCTV clips of the Volvo before and after the collision Footage from a house 60 metres before the junction showed the car travelling at 55mph, the court heard. The speed limit in that area is 40mph, PC Noonan said The officer said he visited the scene shortly after the collision and noted the road was dry with no marks or defects which would have affected driving conditions

candidates.evidence_text: Tameside Hospital Beloved Tameside nurse, 47, dies three days after she's sent home by her NHS colleagues Paula Ivers, 47, died at home three days after attending Tameside General Hospital with chest pain Add to preferred sources Comments News Bethan A children's nurse who was sent home from hospital and told she had acid reflux died just three days later, after doctors failed to consider a life-threatening condition behind her chest pain, a coroner has warned Paula Ivers, 47, died at her home in Denton on March 8, 2024, after attending Tameside General Hospital with severe pain in her chest that was spreading to her back. The mum-of-one had been discharged with a diagnosis acid reflux, but medics had failed to diagnose a tear in the b Now, a coroner has warned that lessons must be learned to prevent future deaths, raising concerns over how patients with chest pain are assessed in hospital and whether vital family medical history is noted Ms Ivers' loved ones said her "needless" death has "left a huge void" in the family. The 19-year-old star's £39,000 custom-plate motor was spotted parked outside the Robin Park Leisure Centre in the town on October 4 - the day before he played at Fellow player Jackson King, 18, took a picture and posted it to the "Parking/Driving Like A Tw** in Wigan !" page on Facebook. "Park like a t*** Luke Littler edition," he wrote Warrington-born Littler, who is nicknamed 'The Nuke', responded saying: "Class that," before explaining in a reply: "No spaces mate so seen the car in front was on the gravel so thought I would join." Other commenters were divided on their opinion of the parking job. Joshua Fulton wrote: "The champ can park where he wants," while Ant Hayton wrote: "Did he park or land it?" Littler's 2025 BMW 120 M Sport, which he reportedly purchased for £39,000, has a top speed of 140 mph and can go from 0 to 60 in 7.8 seconds

All homes are for those over the age of 55 and none The land sits near to the Chew Brook on the edge of Greenfield below the Dovestone Reservoir. The cotton industry mill was built by the Buckley family in 1838 before being bought by the Tanner family in 1919 Over the last century, the mill’s industry moved from cotton mule spinning to tyre cord weaving and dental floss before becoming a local business centre. Now the mill’s owners say the buildings are now at the end of their economic life The mill would be converted into ‘high specification apartments’ with the addition of the fourth floor which was destroyed by fire in 1966. A planning statement said it was ‘a time for change’ and their plans would give the mill ‘a new lease of life’

The cotton industry mill was built by the Buckley family in 1838 before being bought by the Tanner family in 1919 Over the last century, the mill’s industry moved from cotton mule spinning to tyre cord weaving and dental floss before becoming a local business centre. Now the mill’s owners say the buildings are now at the end of their economic life The mill would be converted into ‘high specification apartments’ with the addition of the fourth floor which was destroyed by fire in 1966. A planning statement said it was ‘a time for change’ and their plans would give the mill ‘a new lease of life’

Officers from Greater Manchester Police's Oldham Neighbourhood Team executed a warrant at a property on Broadway at around 4.45am on Wednesday, 14 Octob The operation was led by Neighbourhood Inspector Amie Whitehead and Police Sergeant Tom Layton, with support from the force's Tactical Aid Unit. candidates.evidence_text: Newton Heath Newton Heath murder investigation launched after woman stabbed to death Forensics are working at the scene Add to preferred sources News Stephen Topping Senior reporter , Ramazani Mwamba News reporter and Ludwik Lipiec Apprentice content A murder investigation is underway after a woman was stabbed to death in Newton Heath . Officers were called out to reports of a disturbance on Dorking Avenue at 2am this morning (October 15) Greater Manchester Police says officers found a woman, aged in her 20s, with serious injuries consistent with a stabbing. Tragically, she was pronounced dead at the scene despite the best efforts of emergency services A 25-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of her murder. Officers have also arrested a 61-year-old man and a 38-year-old woman on suspicion of assisting an offender Police and forensics remain at the scene this afternoon, with several streets closed off. A blue forensic tent has been placed in Stapleton Road, while forensic investigators have been gathering extensive evidence from Edmonton Road Part of Briscoe Lane has also been closed off, alongside other nearby streets including Crayford Road. Witnesses described hearing a commotion in the early hours of the morning, including 'screams', moments before a car was caught up in a collision

candidates.evidence_text: Rusholme Leading Manchester school hits out at 'inaccurate' claims as police descend after violence erupts Xaverian College says 'we are aware of speculation and inaccurate information being shared online' Add to preferred sources Comments News Paul B A leading Manchester college has issued a new statement after police were called to a disturbance on its campus during an open day. Footage shared on social media showed police outside 164-year-old Xaverian College in Rusholme last Saturday afternoon Clips shared widely on TikTok showed groups of youths running across a large grassy area in front of the college building. Greater Manchester Police confirmed officers attended at around 1.10pm to reports of a fight and disturbance involving a number of youngers Xaverian College has now moved to provide more detail - and hit out at 'inaccurate information being shared online that does not reflect what happened' The college said there was an 'altercation' involving 'three young visitors, who are not students at the college'. They were removed from the campus. The college said no weapons were involved and there were thankfully no injuries. The college's next open day will go ahead as plan The college's statement said: "Towards the end of our open day on Saturday 10th October 2026, there was an altercation involving three young visitors, who are not students at the college. Staff responded immediately and the individuals were removed from campus

The mum-of-one had been discharged with a diagnosis acid reflux, but medics had failed to diagnose a tear in the b Now, a coroner has warned that lessons must be learned to prevent future deaths, raising concerns over how patients with chest pain are assessed in hospital and whether vital family medical history is noted Ms Ivers' loved ones said her "needless" death has "left a huge void" in the family. candidates.evidence_text: Sale Volvo 'hit speeds of over 40mph' after hitting headteacher and dragging him underneath car, court hears Simon Richardson, 35, is alleged to have knocked Michael Mullins off his bike on the night of April 20 Add to preferred sources News Rachel Sm A man accused of murdering a headteacher drove at speeds of over 40mph with the cyclist trapped beneath his wheels, a jury was told yesterday (October 15) Simon Richardson, 35, is alleged to have knocked Michael Mullins off his bike as he pedalled home from work at Stretford Grammar School, on April 20. But the prosecution at Minshull Street Crown Court say Mr Richardson did not stop and put his foot down, dragging Mr Mullins, 56, Earlier in the trial, witnesses described seeing the Volvo ‘absolutely tanking it’ towards the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane. PC Mark Noonan, a forensic collision investigator for GMP, showed the jury a number of CCTV clips of the Volvo before and after the collision Footage from a house 60 metres before the junction showed the car travelling at 55mph, the court heard. The speed limit in that area is 40mph, PC Noonan said The officer said he visited the scene shortly after the collision and noted the road was dry with no marks or defects which would have affected driving conditions

candidates.evidence_text: Wigan Luke Littler mocked over what he did with his £39k BMW outside a Wigan leisure centre A fellow player jokingly accused him of parking 'like a t**t' Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter and Jack Fifield 05:50, 16 Oc Darts sensation Luke Littler has hit back after a fellow player accused him of parking his BWM 'like a t**t' in Wigan. The 19-year-old star's £39,000 custom-plate motor was spotted parked outside the Robin Park Leisure Centre in the town on October 4 - the day before he played at Fellow player Jackson King, 18, took a picture and posted it to the "Parking/Driving Like A Tw** in Wigan !" page on Facebook. "Park like a t*** Luke Littler edition," he wrote Warrington-born Littler, who is nicknamed 'The Nuke', responded saying: "Class that," before explaining in a reply: "No spaces mate so seen the car in front was on the gravel so thought I would join." Other commenters were divided on their opinion of the parking job. Joshua Fulton wrote: "The champ can park where he wants," while Ant Hayton wrote: "Did he park or land it?" Littler's 2025 BMW 120 M Sport, which he reportedly purchased for £39,000, has a top speed of 140 mph and can go from 0 to 60 in 7.8 seconds

Three people have been arrested in connection with her death Several streets were closed off by police this morning including Edmonton Road and part of Briscoe Lane. Multiple forensic tents have been erected in the area over the course of the day and road closures have been in place Greater Manchester Police (GMP) are urging anyone with any information about the stabbing to come forward. The family have asked for privacy whilst they deal with the devastating loss of their loved one, they added Residents in the area told the Manchester Evening News of the 'screams' that were heard in the early hours of the morning. One resident, speaking anonymously, told of how she heard screams that caused her to rush downstairs and open the front door of her house on Briscoe Lane

candidates.evidence_text: Politics Jodrell Bank promised 'secure future' in major step forward for Manchester Evening News campaign The Manchester Evening News campaign to save science at Jodrell Bank has now reached more than 10,500 signatures Add to preferred sources Comment The Government has promised a "secure future" for Jodrell Bank, following a Manchester Evening News campaign to save space science at the iconic observatory and Lovell Telescope It comes after the future of the near 70-year-old telescope in Cheshire came under threat after funding cuts were announced in July Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds had today (Thursday, October 15) confirmed the government is "exploring" long-term options for the UK's largest telescope He said he recently met representatives from the University of Manchester , which runs the project, in the hope of finding a solution The major update comes as the M.E.N campaign to save science at Jodrell Bank has now reached more than 10,500 signatures

candidates.evidence_text: Dovestones Homes in a unique setting below Dovestone Reservoir could be yours but there's a catch The cotton mill was built by the Buckley family in 1838 before being bought by the Tanner family in 1919 Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Ba An Oldham mill damaged by a fire could be given ‘a new lease of life’ if it is allowed to be converted into flats below Dovestone Reservoir Tanner Bros (Greenfield) Ltd have applied for planning permission at Waterside Mill in Greenfield to demolish ‘poor-quality buildings’, convert the older mill buildings into 59 apartments, and build 26 homes on part of the site. All homes are for those over the age of 55 and none The land sits near to the Chew Brook on the edge of Greenfield below the Dovestone Reservoir. The cotton industry mill was built by the Buckley family in 1838 before being bought by the Tanner family in 1919 Over the last century, the mill’s industry moved from cotton mule spinning to tyre cord weaving and dental floss before becoming a local business centre. Now the mill’s owners say the buildings are now at the end of their economic life The mill would be converted into ‘high specification apartments’ with the addition of the fourth floor which was destroyed by fire in 1966. A planning statement said it was ‘a time for change’ and their plans would give the mill ‘a new lease of life’

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Former supply teacher who took upskirting snaps of female students and used AI to sexualise images jailed for 'horrendous' abuse of trust Abusali Rahman was locked up for six years Add to preferred sources News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 16 A former supply teacher who took upskirting images of girls within schools he worked at and used AI to sexualise images of pupils has been locked up Abusali Rahman, 37, admitted carrying out the ‘horrendous’ abuse of trust. He used a phone to covertly take images of children within the school, and planned to sell the images to other paedophiles online Police discovered that he had taken upskirting images of 12 girls, whose parents were alerted. It is understood that he placed his iPhone in the top pocket of his clothing in order to capture the images Greater Manchester Police said the girls were aged between 13 and 16, and attended seven high schools across Bury, Bolton and Salford. In all, Rahman had taught at 25 schools across the North West In addition to the upskirting, Rahman stole images of girls he had taught from their social media profiles, before using AI to create sexualised images and post them on social media

Officers were called out to reports of a disturbance on Dorking Avenue at 2am this morning (October 15) Greater Manchester Police says officers found a woman, aged in her 20s, with serious injuries consistent with a stabbing. Tragically, she was pronounced dead at the scene despite the best efforts of emergency services A 25-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of her murder. Officers have also arrested a 61-year-old man and a 38-year-old woman on suspicion of assisting an offender Police and forensics remain at the scene this afternoon, with several streets closed off. A blue forensic tent has been placed in Stapleton Road, while forensic investigators have been gathering extensive evidence from Edmonton Road Part of Briscoe Lane has also been closed off, alongside other nearby streets including Crayford Road. Witnesses described hearing a commotion in the early hours of the morning, including 'screams', moments before a car was caught up in a collision

Officers from Greater Manchester Police's Oldham Neighbourhood Team executed a warrant at a property on Broadway at around 4.45am on Wednesday, 14 Octob The operation was led by Neighbourhood Inspector Amie Whitehead and Police Sergeant Tom Layton, with support from the force's Tactical Aid Unit. Add to preferred sources Comments News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 05:53, 15 Oct 2026 Updated 07:05, 15 Oct 202 A visitor to Manchester says he has been left 'helpless' and 'homeless' after his luxury city centre studio became infested with bedbugs The man, who asked to remain anonymous, told the Manchester Evening News of a nightmare experience at a flat in the Swan Street House complex in the Northern Quarter . A medical professional and originally from Birmingham, he travelled to work an study in the city After a fortnight in the region, he decided to book himself a short stay at the deluxe high-rise on Mason Street. He told the MEN his 12-day stay cost £1,634 when he booked it online. But after just one evening, he claims to have woke up with bug bites all over his body The property is understood to have offered the individual a refund since the incident. He said: "After the first day, I got a few rashes on my body so I went to the housekeeping and they came and changed my bedding "The second night it was more obvious, I thought there was something that doesn't look right. I called the housekeeping again and they did the same thing. But I wasn't convinced, I thought there was something more than that. So, I removed the mattress and it was full of bedbugs."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Man arrested after police seize over £340,000 worth of illegal vapes and drugs at Bolton properties The man has been arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of class B drugs Add to preferred sources Comments News Charlotte Fisher A man has been arrested after police seized over £340,000 worth of illegal vapes, drugs, and suspected cannabis oil at two properties in Bolton earlier this week. The total value of the items is estimated to be over £349,700 It comes after officers from Greater Manchester Police , in partnership with Trading Standards and Bolton Council, raided two properties on Chorley Old Road and Bentinck Street on Monday (October 12) Over 25,000 single use vapes were seized, amounting to approximately £12,700 in street value, and over 3,500 bottles of vape liquid was also obtained Police also seized 500 bottles of suspected cannabis oil, valued at around £25,000, along with 100kg of CBD powder, estimated to be worth £60,000 The man, aged 45, has been arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of class B drugs. He since been released on bail, pending further enquiries

Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

candidates.lead: Buju Architects is leading on design.
candidates.evidence_text: Buju Architects is leading on design. Credit: via planning documents A group of local business owners has worked up proposals for a residential scheme on the site of the dilapidated Compstall Mill The 141-home proposal, lodged in outline with Stockport Council, come almost 20 years since Ask put forward plans to redevelop the derelict 19th-century Stockport industrial complex Compstall Mill 2025, whose directors are Sarah Jackson, Michael Clark, Philip Newton, Thomas Simpson, acquired the site next to Etherow Country Park at auction last year from Euro Property Investments with the intention of revamping the four-acre site off Andrew Street in Compsta New-build homes would be constructed along Andrew Street while Albert and Victoria mills would be converted into apartments The two retained buildings, Victoria Mill and the Gatehouse, will be converted into 39 and six apartments respectively. The arson-damaged Albert Mill is to be demolished and replaced with a building featuring 48 flats

The year-long programme celebrates the people, places and stories that have helped shape the city over the last century Mark E Smith, who was born in Broughton, was the founder and frontman of influential post-punk band The Fall. Renowned for his distinctive voice, uncompromising creativity and unique perspective, Mark E Smith became one of the most influential figures in British alternative music The mural was created by Mark Kennedy, who has spent more than three decades creating major public art projects across Greater Manchester and Salford The artwork is based on a photograph Kennedy took while walking through Heaton Park with Mark E Smith following a meeting about artwork for The Fall’s Your Future Our Clutter album. candidates.evidence_text: Police appeal after £10,000 air conditioning units stolen from Altrincham opticians Skip to content News — Police, Fire & Court Police appeal after £10,000 air conditioning units stolen from Altrincham opticians Police have released an image of the two men they wish to speak to. , and David Prior October 15, 2026 . 5:42 PM 1 min read Share on Twitter Share on Facebook Share on Pinterest Share on LinkedIn Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Police are appealing for information after two air conditioning units worth a total of £10,000 were stolen from an opticians in Altrincham town centre. The units were taken from Maskell + Josephson opticians on Regent Road in the early hours of Tuesday 6 October. Greater Manchester Police said two men were seen entering a courtyard behind the business carrying cutters between 11.10am and 11.20am on Monday 5 October. The men subsequently left the courtyard, after which the air conditioning units reportedly fell from the wall. The two men police want to speak to Police believe the same two men returned to the courtyard at around 6am the following morning and removed the two units. Officers have released images of two men they would like to speak to in connection with the theft, as they believe they could assist with their enquiries. Anyone with information is asked to contact GMP on 101 or via LiveChat, quoting crime reference CRI/06MM/0015143/26. candidates.evidence_text: The report also proposes charges at Thorley Lane car park in Timperley, which is currently free Share on WhatsApp Share via Email The report proposes charges at Thorley Lane car park in Timperley, which is currently free Motorists in Altrincham could face parking charges until 8pm and on Sundays under new proposals put forward by Trafford Council The changes form part of the council's draft budget for 2027/28, which aims to raise an additional £250,000 a year from parking charges across the borough The proposals include extending on-street charging hours in Altrincham, Sale and parts of Stretford, alongside revised tariffs for council-owned car parks, the introduction of Sunday charging and extended charging hours from 8am to 8pm In Altrincham, council-operated car parks include Regent Road and Oakfield Road, while nearby council car parks include Cecil Road, Victoria Road and Brown Street in Hale, and Balmoral Road and Baker Street in Timperley Currently, charges at these car parks generally apply between 8am and 6pm, Monday to Saturday, with parking free on Sundays

evidence_packet.summary: Right at Home South Trafford and Wyncourt Nursing Home staged a joint picnic at Wyncourt
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Right at Home South Trafford and Wyncourt Nursing Home staged a joint picnic at Wyncourt Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Two Outstanding-rated Timperley care providers have joined forces for the first time to raise money for dementia Right at Home South Trafford and Wyncourt Nursing Home staged a joint picnic at Wyncourt this summer in aid of Dementia Adventure, Right at Home’s charity partner. It was the first collaboration of its kind for either organisation “It was a brilliant day. Absolutely fantastic,” says Vicki Hobson-Middleton, activities coordinator at Wyncourt Wyncourt’s garden was dressed for the occasion, with balloons, tombola, bingo, noughts and crosses and ring toss. Family members donated cakes, the home’s chef made more, and there were sandwiches on the tables. Relatives came over, staff joined in and the weather held “Everybody got involved,” Vicki says. “I was really worried about the weather, but it was just absolutely stunning.”

candidates.evidence_text: It's one of the longest-running sagas in the town Share on WhatsApp Share via Email One of Altrincham's longest-running regeneration sagas could be entering a new chapter, with Trafford Council proposing to turn the former Altair site into a major residential development The council is recommending that the 4.5-acre site between Oakfield Road and Moss Lane should be developed primarily for housing, potentially bringing an end to almost two decades of failed plans for a major new shopping, leisure and residential quarter The proposals, which will be considered by Trafford Council's Executive on Monday October 19, would also see the existing surface car park potentially replaced by a multi-storey parking and transport hub An indicative masterplan includes apartment buildings of five storeys or more, smaller residential blocks, commercial space and landscaped communal areas The plans represent a significant change of direction for the site, which was originally earmarked for the £70 million Altair development first unveiled in 2008

candidates.evidence_text: They said they were "deeply saddened" by the decision to adopt the motion Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Altrincham's Green councillors Dan Jerrome, Geraldine Coggins and Michael Welton Green councillors in Trafford have publicly distanced themselves from their national party's controversial new policy on Zionism, warning that it could negatively af In a strongly worded statement, seven Green councillors, including representatives of Altrincham, said they were "deeply saddened" by the decision to adopt the motion at the party's national conference on Sunday The motion, entitled Zionism is Racism , was passed by 1,022 votes to 813 at the Green Party conference in Brighton It formally establishes the Greens as an anti-Zionist party, defines Zionism as a form of racism and supports the creation of a single democratic Palestinian state across historic Palestine, with Jerusalem as its capital But Trafford's Green councillors have made clear they oppose aspects of the policy, particularly its position on Palestinian statehood and its definition of Zionism

candidates.recovery_refetched_evidence: Brand new Family Hub opens in Harpurhey to help give local children best start in life | Manchester City Council Remembering Councillor Pat Karney Leave a message in our online book of condolence . × Close alert Brand new Family Hub opens in Harpurhey to help give local children best start in life Thursday 15 October 2026 A brand-new family hub has opened in Harpurhey this week to help ensure local children and young people are given the very best start in life and helped to become happy and healthy young adults who achieve their full potential. The Best Start in Life Family Hub - Harpurhey, is located inside North City Leisure Centre on Upper Conran Street and provides one-stop-shop style access to a wide range of advice and support for parents and carers, as well as children and young people. Its welcoming and accessible space gives families open-door access to services including family support, parenting programmes, and support for children who have special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), alongside health and wellbeing activities and community connections. Designed to support families with children aged 0–19 years (up to 25 years for SEND and care leavers), as well as expectant parents, the team at the centre can provide information, advice, guidance, and practical support - helping families access services both within the Hub and across the local neighbourhood in partnership with schools and community organisations. The kind of support and guidance on offer to families at the Hub begins from even before a child is born with pregnancy support and information for expectant parents, taking in every stage of childhood after that once a child is born - from feeding guidance and breastfeeding support, early language and learning, perinatal mental health support and parenting groups, to help with school applications, managing behaviour, and support for families new to the area, along with information about adult learning opportunities, volunteering, work experience and much more. Staff at the Hub can also help families with form -filling and referrals to other agencies for additional support such as housing, counselling, and benefits advice. The Harpurhey Family Hub is the sixth such Family Hub to open in Manchester and follows the opening of other hubs over the last two years in Longsight, Wythenshawe, Cheetham Hill, Gorton and Clayton. One parent who is already a big fan of the Hub is local mum Shelter who has been a regular at the Hub with her 6-month-old daughter Nahla since it first opened its doors to parents and is really valuing the support she gets there including from other mums. She said: "This is my first child and I never knew that you needed to be outside with other mums. Just to be with other women who are going through the same thing - like some parents have three children so they can give you advice on stuff that you don't know, things they've been doing with their kids at home to reach their skills like sitting, eating, anything else. "So it's very good to meet other people, you can make friends for yourself and your own mental health, and babies get to see other babies doing stuff and play with them and make friends, so I think it's very good for their brain development and I've really loved it." The Harpurhey Family Hub's opening follows publication earlier this year by the council of its Best Start in Life strategy which outlines how the city plans to support families with babies and children up to school age over the coming years, and also comes hot on the heels of Manchester's recent recognition by UNICEF as a Child Friendly City. Councillor Julie Reid, Executive Member for Early Years, Children and Young People, Manchester City Council, said: "We're determined to make sure that every child in Manchester has the very best start in life and grows up safe, healthy, and happy. "Our Best Start in Life Family Hubs have a vital part to play in this with their one-stop-shop approach to supporting families with whatever kind of help and advice they may need and at whatever point in their child's life. "With six Family Hubs now open and more to come over the course of the next year, they are already making a huge difference to our families in the city and to the life chances of our children and young people." candidates.evidence_text: Work is set to start on high quality, safe and attractive walking and cycling improvements in Bolton town centre, after Bolton Council secured over £5m of funding The major upgrades aim to make every-day journeys simpler and more enjoyable and add to the ongoing regeneration of the town centre Phase one of the scheme will focus on Bradshawgate and Great Moor Street Roads will be resurfaced and footpaths repaved to make them more attractive and benefit people travelling on foot There will be changes at side roads to give pedestrians priority, along with an upgraded pedestrian crossing on Bradshawgate near Nelson Square Four junctions will be upgraded to make it easier and safer for people on foot and riding bikes to travel around the town centre

candidates.evidence_text: Press release — 9 October 2026 12:24 Share Share this story Copy link Link copied! Download A major investment in specialist education has been completed at Millwood Primary School, creating additional places and state-of-the-art facilities for children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) in Bury The £13 million project has delivered a substantial new wing containing seven new classrooms, a multi-use hall, sensory rooms, a rebound room, non-teaching areas, external play spaces and additional car parking. The project has also included repairs to the school's roof and exist The scheme has been funded through capital allocations from the Department for Education which supports local authorities in their duty to provide suitable school placements for children and young people with SEND Creating more capacity at Millwood is a key part of Bury Council's plans to strengthen SEND provision across the borough. The expansion responds to increasing demand for specialist school places and will enable more children and young people to have their needs met closer to home The new facilities allow Millwood to cater for more than 200 primary-aged pupils with a range of additional educational needs and disabilities, providing high-quality learning environments designed to support pupils to thrive and achieve their full potential

candidates.evidence_text: Young people from across the borough came together to explore how our collective green journeys can create a more sustainable future for all Organised by Wigan Council’s Climate Response team, the Youth Climate Summit returned to The Edge for the fifth time on Wednesday, 30th September, bringing together pupils from primary schools, secondary schools, and colleges for an event focusing on this year’s theme of green jo The theme encouraged attendees to think about their own path to sustainability, how they can make better choices, and how we can all work together to find solutions to the climate crisis Councillor Paul Kenny, portfolio holder for planning, environmental service, and transport, said: “It’s fantastic that so many young people at the Youth Climate Summit came together to learn about sustainability and how they can have a positive impact on the environment “The green journeys theme is particularly important as it highlights that although we may all start at different places, or follow different paths, we can all work towards a common goal “That common goal should be how we can improve people’s lives, find solutions to the climate crisis, and ensure our planet is habitable for generations to come, and it was inspiring to see so many young people engaging with this important message.”

candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . Tickets . . . . . . . Ruby Turner is widely recognised as one of the UK’s leading soul singers, known for her powerful performances across soul, R&B, and reggae. She has earned praise not only for her solo albums and live shows but also for her frequent collaborations with Jools Holland’s Rhythm & Blues Orchestra. . . Ruby Turner began a successful run as a solo artist in the late 1980s, landing a chart-topping hit with "It's Gonna Be Alright," and releasing numerous respected albums and singles over the coming years that traversed soul, gospel, and pop. She became a frequent collaborator with Jools Holland and performed with an array of high-profile stars from Mick Jagger to Steve Winwood. . . Her debut album, Woman Hold Up Half the Sky (1986), was a critical and commercial success, and she went on to release another 13 albums over the course of the next three decades, including 1989's Paradise, which peaked at number 39 on the Billboard R&B chart. She also charted eight singles throughout the 80s and 90s, the most successful of which was "I'd Rather Go Blind". . . On 4 June 2012 Ruby performed 'You Are So Beautiful' with Jools Holland at the Queen's Diamond Jubilee Concert outside Buckingham Palace in London. In autumn 2012, Ruby was a guest judge on the BBC's The Choir: Sing While You Work with choirmaster Gareth Malone and in 2013 Ruby was a guest judge on the BBC's Songs of Praise Gospel Choirs competition. In June 2016 Ruby was awarded an MBE. . . . . . candidates.evidence_text: Dame Meera Syal joins us to share the hilarious and heartwarming true stories that have shaped her life and work as one of Britain’s most beloved comedy legends Growing up in the only Asian family in a West Midlands mining village, Meera Syal wanted to take the stage long before anyone was ready to listen As one of the creators of Goodness Gracious Me, she changed British comedy forever. As the indomitable Granny Ummi, she terrified the guests visiting The Kumars at Number 42. She’s topped the pop charts, been a Professor at Oxford, and written a musical with Andrew Lloyd Webber. candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club, or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! Following their acclaimed album elllegy (RTÉ Radio 1 Best Group), The Olllam has collaborated with GRAMMY-nominated producer Zedd, shared the stage in Belfast with actor Anthony Boyle (Netflix’s House of Guinness), and recently completed a landmark U.S. tour in November 2025. From ancient airs to future soundscapes, The Olllam is not just carrying the tradition forward—they’re reinventing it

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Olllam is a band that fuses Irish traditional music with the modern jazz/post-rock energy of Detroit. Led by uilleann piper John McSherry, the band features Joe Dart (Vulfpeck), Michael Shimmin, Ross Ainslie, Seán O’Meara, and Joe Hettinga. Following their acclaimed album elllegy (RTÉ Radio 1 Best Group), The Olllam has collaborated with GRAMMY-nominated producer Zedd, shared the stage in Belfast with actor Anthony Boyle (Netflix’s House of Guinness), and recently completed a landmark U.S. tour in November 2025. From ancient airs to future soundscapes, The Olllam is not just carrying the tradition forward—they’re reinventing it

candidates.evidence_text: This year's nominations for Manchester's best bar, best restaurant and best chef are now open Go to Manchester's Finest X profile The Manchester Food and Drink Festival (MFDF) Awards have revealed their 2026 shortlists, with some of Greater Manchester’s best-known restaurants, bars, pubs, cafés and independent food businesses among the nominees The awards ceremony will take place on Monday 25 January 2027, moving to City Hall at Medlock Square for the first time. The new entertainment district is home to a growing collection of bars and restaurants, including Zadie’s and Little Beast Sponsored by Therme Manchester, the awards will recognise businesses and individuals across 17 categories, covering everything from affordable eats and neighbourhood venues to independent producers and the region’s leading chefs Among those competing for Restaurant of the Year are Kallos, Stow, Higher Ground, Winsome, Erst, The Pearl, Adam Reid at The French and The Trof The Chef of the Year shortlist includes Jamie Pickles of Stow, Shaun Moffatt of Winsome, Jess Furniss of WTLGI, Gary Weir of Open Fire and Tartuffe, Sian Wilson of Bar Posie, Tom Barnes of Skof, Rosie Maguire of Higher Ground and Brit Wardle of 10 Tib Lane

candidates.evidence_text: The LGBTQ+ bar returns on Tariff Street with cocktails, food, live jazz, drag and late-night DJ sets By Manchester's Finest, Last updated 14 October 2026 Go to Manchester's Finest X profile LGBTQ+ cocktail bar Red Light will reopen in Manchester’s Northern Quarter on Friday 9 October, taking over a new space on Tariff Street The bar, founded by Deana Ferguson, will return next door to The Whisky Jar with a new look, an expanded food and drink menu and a programme of live music, DJs and performance The new Red Light features booth seating, a bar and club-style space, red lighting and an outdoor terrace, which will remain open until 11pm. Its interiors will also showcase work from queer local photographers Jen Melia, Sara Carpentieri, Nick Priestley and Harmeet Singh A number of cocktails from Red Light’s original menu will return, including the Pink Picante and Pomme Verte, its take on an appletini. Other returning drinks include the Belfast Coffee, spicy pickle martini Especiado and Pornstar Chic, made with homemade passionfruit sorbet

The orchard and nearby bee and butterfly garden, have been designed to attract wildlife The Peel Learning Garden, supported by The Peel Group, will help schoolchildren learn how plants affect our lives and the planet, whilst the Community Wellbeing Garden provides a space for people to garden, socialise and relax

evidence_packet.evidence_text: One of Stockport's best free days out is back on Saturday 10th October. From 10am to 4pm, The Makers Market takes over Market Place, right in the heart of SK1, with 65+ independent traders selling handmade goods, artisan food and one-off finds against the backdrop of Stockport's Think craft, ceramics, prints, jewellery, candles, street food, and the kind of things you won't find anywhere else. It's a good chance to get some early Christmas shopping done too. Entry's free, it's dog-friendly and there's seating on-site, so you can take your time having a m Getting there: Stockport Interchange is the nearest bus stop, about a 12-minute walk away. There are cycle racks on-site. Parking nearby is limited, so check Parkopedia for the closest spaces 🗓 Saturday 10 October, 10am to 4pm (second Saturday of every month)

candidates.evidence_text: L-R: Simon Shaw, Anna Dick, Alastair Brown, Tripti Anil, Alan Jackson Simon Shaw, Delivery Director at Codurance, hosted the lunchtime session for tech leaders and introduced Codurance, which is a global software engineering consultancy that has run its Manchester office for 15 years He was joined on the panel by Anna Dick, Chief Technology & Product Officer at Capsule; Alastair Brown, Group Director of AI and Technology at Peninsula; Tripti Anil, Senior Leader, Data & Analytics at Kellanova; and Alan Jackson, Director of Client Solutions at Codurance Talking about discovering how AI can be used in projects, Anna said that Capsule's initial three months of AI exploration across all its business teams built appetite for further experimentation, but it also got a little out of control. Some things needed revisiting and tidying u Alastair stressed product discipline in order to understand the business driver and the outcome you want. At Peninsula, one initiative focused on giving customers richer answers and delivered over £1m in revenue. He said success depends on strong sponsorship and expertise from wi Tripti described spending three years building data foundations at Kellanova, focusing on "the right things at the right time" and bringing business teams along on the journey. They started with UK field sales as a proof of concept initially

candidates.evidence_text: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, backing businesses to grow and taking some of what has worked in Greater Manchester into a wider national approach. He also confirmed that AI will be a central focus of the That felt particularly relevant following an event we hosted through the UK Tech Cluster Group with AI Minister Kanishka Narayan, North East Mayor Kim McGuinness and other regional leaders, looking at AI, devolution and local growth One of the clearest themes from the discussion was that devolution should not mean every place trying to build the same thing. Different regions have different strengths, assets and specialisms, and there was a strong view that greater collaboration between places could create bi Procurement and buying local also featured strongly. The discussion highlighted the role public sector buying power can play in supporting regional businesses, helping successful pilots move into commercial contracts and strengthening UK capability in areas such as AI and cyber There was also a broader conversation about sovereignty and the UK’s role internationally. The discussion was not about trying to own every part of the AI stack, but about understanding where the UK already has genuine capability and where it makes sense to build more. Strengths

candidates.summary: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised
candidates.reason: LLM-review: Акции Nvidia упали на 3,4%, SoftBank на 10,7% после слов Амодеи об ИИ | Validator: previous publication found on 2026-10-15; plan-digest will make the final repeat decision (provisional=exact_fingerprint_unchanged_evidence, anchor=local_action, ttl=1d). | Selection: Selected in tech_business shortlist before writing.
candidates.practical_angle: Есть обновление, которое может быть полезно в сегодняшней сводке.
candidates.lead: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing.
candidates.evidence_text: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised. More capital is being concentrated in fewer companies while the market for exits remains difficult Financial news recently added another dimension to that discussion. AI-related shares fell last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower approach to the development of increasingly capable AI models. Nvidia finished the day down 3.4%, SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo Additionally, the Bank of England is predicted to increase interest rates later this year, which could affect the North West's tech funding landscape by raising the cost of capital across the board, compressing valuations, pushing investors toward profitability over growth-at-all The British Business Bank's 2026 Small Business Equity Tracker found that equity investment into UK smaller businesses fell 4% to £12.3bn in 2025. Seed deal numbers fell 27% and venture deals fell 13%. AI companies attracted 44% of all investment into smaller businesses while the Beauhurst recorded £14.4bn of UK equity investment across 2,799 deals in the first half of 2026 but three AI companies accounted for 29% of all the capital raised. Those very large rounds can make the overall market look stronger than it feels to businesses raising at seed or Ser Beauhurst's analysis shows that UK equity investment more than doubled between 2017 and 2021 to £32.2bn while annual exits remained at around 400 to 500. An exit takes a median of four years from a funding round

Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

candidates.lead: Bolton Car Boot Sale at Bolton Car Boot Sale
candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. However, their wedding party in Italy, planned for a year later, never took place last summer, and they ended their eight- He is now dating another Dutch model, Amber Yuusef, confirming their relationship in June. De Ligt's ex-wife has now spoken at length about their breakup Molenaar appeared on the first episode of an online interview series on YouTube with Robbert Rodenburg, titled 'Guncle'. She said: "It has been a tough year, a year with a lot of change, but also a year for which I am very grateful." Speaking for the first time about the end of her relationship with De Ligt, the model said: "We have had a very nice time all these years, and yet last year we came to the conclusion that it is no longer there in the romantic way."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: 8 ноября 2026 года в Indigo at The O2 состоится концерт GORAN BREGOVIC в Лондоне Имя Горана Бреговича давно стало символом целого музыкального мира. Сотрудничество с режиссером Emir Kusturica подарило мировому кинематографу саундтреки, ставшие неотъемлемой частью фильмов Time of the Gypsies, Arizona Dream и Underground. Его главный талант — превращать народные мотивы в современное искусство, не теряя их подлинной силы.
